summary: Redwood reviewed data residency and region pinning options for CardioSafe (healthcare customer). Main concerns: EU data residency, cross-border processing, sub-processor disclosure, SSO/SAML integration, KMS/encryption, and audit logs. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs, and next steps include sharing SOC2/ISO artifacts, SAML guides, and a follow-up private deployment feasibility call.
topics: KMS and encryption at rest/in transit
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Khan (CardioSafe Head of Compliance), Markus Engel (CardioSafe Cloud Architect), Sofia Ruiz (CardioSafe Legal)
---
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time right before the holidays. Quick intros, and then Carlos will run through how we handle data residency and region pinning.
[00:10] Aisha (CardioSafe): Hi all, Aisha here. We're specifically worried about EU patient data and making sure tokens or PII never leave EU processing zones.
[00:18] Markus (CardioSafe): Yep, and from infra perspective we need deterministic routing, ideally region pinning per tenant. We're evaluating hosted but may need a private or dedicated approach.
[00:26] Carlos (Redwood SE): Great — quick agenda: region pinning, cross-border fallbacks, sub-processor list, encryption/KMS, and SSO/SAML details. I'll cover the runtime behavior and failover patterns.
[00:35] Sofia (CardioSafe): Also, legal will want sub-processor disclosures and the flow diagram showing where data leaves EU, if at all.
[00:42] Carlos (Redwood SE): Totally. So first, region pinning in the hosted product: we allow tenant-level region preferences — you can pin traffic to EU regions (for example Frankfurt or Amsterdam) which ensures inference and short-term logs are processed in-region. We do have cross-border fallback policies when capacity is constrained; those are configurable and require explicit approval for cross-border processing.
[00:58] Aisha (CardioSafe): When you say "short-term logs," are you referring to request/response capture for debugging? What's retained and where?
[01:06] Carlos (Redwood SE): Good question. By default we capture minimal operational logs (latency, errors) and we offer configurable transcript retention. For customers that need EU-only retention we can configure retention to keep logs in-region and ship audit logs to your S3 in the EU. Note: some debug artifacts (stack traces) may still be generated but we avoid sending payload to external regions unless explicitly allowed.
[01:30] Markus (CardioSafe): How about KV cache — like the KV cash or cache — where does the KV live?
[01:36] Carlos (Redwood SE): KV cache is regional; KV cache and prefix caching are colocated with the inference pods. We don't shard that across regions unless you configure multi-region and accept cross-border replication.
[01:45] Lena (Redwood AE): Just to add, we have a dedicated offering and a private deployment. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity within a cloud region and stronger isolation, while Private lets you run a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem for full data residency guarantees.
[02:00] Aisha (CardioSafe): Private would be ideal from a compliance standpoint, but it's heavier. Can you outline what the typical blockers are?
[02:08] Carlos (Redwood SE): For private, blockers are usually network/firewall config, KMS integration (bring-your-own-key), and routing to your storage. We provide an installer and a documented network requirements sheet. Latency is no problem since it's in your VPC, but operational overhead is higher.
[02:24] Markus (CardioSafe): For BYOK, do you integrate with AWS KMS & HSM, or do you require a specific provider?
[02:30] Carlos (Redwood SE): We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-HSM flows. Keys can be customer-managed; we perform envelope encryption with platform keys only for control plane metadata. All data-at-rest and in-transit encryption is enforced.
[02:45] Sofia (CardioSafe): On sub-processors, can you provide a current list and whether any third parties process data outside EU? We need that for our DPIA.
[02:53] Lena (Redwood AE): Yes — we'll share the sub-processor list. Major infra providers (AWS, GCP) are listed; we also use a CDN and a monitoring vendor, both of which have EU regions. We'll send the detailed doc.
[03:04] Aisha (CardioSafe): What about SOC2 and ISO? We require evidence for both.
[03:08] Lena (Redwood AE): We have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates. I'll attach the latest reports — redacted where appropriate — in the follow-up.
[03:15] Markus (CardioSafe): Let's talk about cross-border fallbacks: if you pin to EU and a burst overload happens, do you failover to US? That's a non-starter unless we explicitly approve.
[03:25] Carlos (Redwood SE): Right — our default policy favors availability with controlled fallbacks, but for regulated customers we can configure strict no-cross-border rules which will queue or throttle instead of failing over. That does increase latency risk during capacity peaks.
[03:40] Aisha (CardioSafe): Could you estimate the cost/latency tradeoff? If you throttle during peaks vs failover, what's the real-world impact?
[03:49] Carlos (Redwood SE): Rough ballpark: if you disable cross-border failover and cap to EU capacity, you might see increased tail latency during 99.9 percentile spikes and potential throttling. Cost isn't directly higher, but UX could be impacted; for predictable load we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll provide concrete numbers based on your QPS.
[04:10] Lena (Redwood AE): Also worth noting: we can do a small pilot on Dedicated capacity reserved in EU for a short POC to show behavior under load.
[04:18] Markus (CardioSafe): For SSO, we use SAML 2.0 and want SCIM user provisioning and fine-grained RBAC. How does Redwood map roles and how are audit logs exposed?
[04:28] Carlos (Redwood SE): We support SAML 2.0 single sign-on and SCIM for provisioning. Roles map to RBAC policies; you can define admin, dev, viewer, etc. Audit logs (auth, admin actions, API keys) can be streamed to customer-managed logging (e.g., CloudWatch, Stackdriver, or S3) in-region.
[04:44] Sofia (CardioSafe): Are API keys ever visible to Redwood personnel?
[04:48] Carlos (Redwood SE): No, API keys are hashed; we store key material only as one-way hashes and we never log full keys. For private deployments, keys remain in your control.
[04:56] Aisha (CardioSafe): How do you handle data subject requests and deletion requests across backups and caches?
[05:02] Carlos (Redwood SE): We have retention controls and purge flows. For cached KV entries we have TTLs and explicit deletion endpoints; for backups we follow an RPO/RTO schedule and can do targeted deletion requests — we'll detail the process in the data handling doc.
[05:18] Lena (Redwood AE): Quick note on sub-processors: if any sub-processor introduces cross-border processing we flag it in the sub-processor list and notify customers with a 30-day window where possible.
[05:27] Markus (CardioSafe): Can you provide the EU data flow diagram — egress points, control plane, telemetry destinations?
[05:32] Lena (Redwood AE): Yes, we'll share a diagram showing control plane traffic and data plane separation.
[05:38] [Short silence as Carlos pulls up a diagram link]
[05:45] Carlos (Redwood SE): I'm sharing a link in the chat to the region-pinning doc (note: link omitted in transcript) — high-level: requests hit the regional gateway, are routed to regional inference pools; audit logs can be pushed to your EU bucket; control plane metadata may communicate with our management plane but we can reduce that footprint for private deployments.
[06:05] Aisha (CardioSafe): Anything to call out about encryption in transit? TLS 1.2/1.3? Mutual TLS for internal?
[06:12] Carlos (Redwood SE): We require TLS 1.2+ for public endpoints and optionally mTLS for private endpoints. Internal traffic between services is encrypted, and for private deployments we support VPC peering and private endpoints only.
[06:24] Sofia (CardioSafe): From a legal perspective, we'll need Data Processing Addendum language around subprocessors and a clause prohibiting non-approved cross-border processing. Is that standard?
[06:33] Lena (Redwood AE): We have DPA templates with options. For enterprise customers we negotiate specific clauses; we'll share standard DPA and we can flag the cross-border clause for discussion.
[06:43] Markus (CardioSafe): If we do Dedicated in EU, can we get SLA guarantees on region-only processing?
[06:49] Carlos (Redwood SE): Dedicated gives stronger guarantees for processing locality and capacity caps. We'll surface explicit contract language in the offer. Private gives the strongest isolation since control plane can be customer-managed.
[06:58] Aisha (CardioSafe): For monitoring/observability, can we control retention windows? We need audit logs for 7 years for certain events.
[07:06] Carlos (Redwood SE): We can export logs to your storage with configurable retention. For platform-managed logs, retention policies are configurable up to X years (we'll confirm the maximum in the follow-up).
[07:18] Lena (Redwood AE): Okay I want to make sure we capture the ask: CardioSafe wants EU-only processing unless explicitly approved, needs SOC2/ISO evidence, sub-processor list and flow diagram, SAML+SCIM integration docs, and a region-pinning config + cost/latency estimate.
[07:31] Aisha (CardioSafe): That's correct. Also, a proof-of-concept on Dedicated in EU for a week or two would be helpful.
[07:38] Carlos (Redwood SE): We can arrange a POC on Dedicated EU capacity; it requires a short setup and reserved infra. We'll follow up with sizing questions.
[07:46] Sofia (CardioSafe): Legal will review DPA template once we get it. We'll also want to know if Redwood uses any sub-processors that do machine learning model training outside the EU.
[07:55] Carlos (Redwood SE): We don't train customer data; model training uses separate corp pipelines and customer data is not used. We'll state that in the sub-processor doc.
[08:04] Lena (Redwood AE): Great — we'll share artifacts after the call. Any last technical Qs?
[08:09] Markus (CardioSafe): One small one — how do you handle telemetry that helps you optimize routing? Is any of that exported?
[08:15] Carlos (Redwood SE): Telemetry is aggregated and anonymized; for EU pinned customers we keep telemetry scoped to region and can provide aggregated metrics.
[08:24] Aisha (CardioSafe): Thanks, that helps.
[08:27] Lena (Redwood AE): Alright, recap of next steps in chat, I'll attach SOC2 and ISO, Carlos will send region-pinning examples and latency/cost notes, and we'll schedule the private/dedicated POC call for early Jan.
[08:42] Sofia (CardioSafe): Thanks everyone, appreciate the thoroughness.
[08:47] Carlos (Redwood SE): Thanks all, we'll follow up with docs.
[08:50] Lena (Redwood AE): Bye.
